subject.title: System prompt should prefer Skill tool over read when available

question: Should native OpenClaw prompt guidance prefer a plugin-provided `Skill` tool by raw tool name, or only prefer a loader that advertises an explicit trusted skill-loading capability?
rationale: The requested behavior changes instruction authority from direct file reads to plugin tool responses, which is a product/security boundary rather than a mechanical prompt edit.

options.title: Require Explicit Loader Capability
options.body: Add or reuse a generic plugin capability/manifest/runtime marker and have prompt guidance prefer only that approved loader, preserving read fallback for other tools named Skill.

options.title: Adopt Tool-Name Convention
options.body: Treat normalized `Skill`/`skill` tool availability as the supported contract and document that convention for plugin authors.

options.title: Wait For Router Direction
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers decide whether the `local_skill_route` design should replace direct Skill-tool preference.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Loader Capability
recommendation.body: Add or reuse a generic plugin capability/manifest/runtime marker and have prompt guidance prefer only that approved loader, preserving read fallback for other tools named Skill.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced/tightened the skills prompt surface and owns the active local-router PR closest to this design choice.
